top_level_objectives: Represent physical quantities as vectors with magnitude and direction
Add vectors tip-to-tail and interpret the resultant
Resolve a vector into horizontal and vertical components using right-triangle trigonometry
Explain how projectile motion combines independent horizontal and vertical motions
Predict how launch angle and launch speed affect trajectory, range, and maximum height

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient students to vectors as directed quantities and connect their geometry to physical meaning.
key_visuals: A coordinate plane with two labeled arrows of different lengths and directions
On-screen labels for magnitude, direction, and components
A clean comparison between a scalar and a vector
student_actions: Inspect the arrows and identify which features describe size and which describe direction
Select a vector and note how changing its length or angle changes its representation

scenes.brief_purpose: Show that vectors combine by placing them head-to-tail and drawing the resultant from start to finish.
key_visuals: Two vectors arranged tip-to-tail on the plane
A resultant arrow drawn from the first tail to the final tip
A simple triangle or parallelogram depiction supporting the addition
student_actions: Arrange or compare vectors so they add tip-to-tail
Predict the resultant direction and magnitude before revealing the sum

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students see how one vector can be represented by horizontal and vertical components on chosen axes.
key_visuals: A single diagonal vector with dashed horizontal and vertical projections
Right-angle markers showing the component triangle
Labels for x-component, y-component, magnitude, and angle
student_actions: Choose an angle or inspect one given vector and determine its components
Use the triangle relationship to connect the vector’s magnitude with its x and y parts

scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to the initial velocity of a projectile launched at an angle.
key_visuals: A projectile launcher aimed upward at an angle
An initial velocity arrow with visible horizontal and vertical components
A projected path beginning from the launch point
student_actions: Adjust the launch angle and speed, then observe how the initial velocity splits into components
Compare different launches and identify which component is larger in each case

scenes.brief_purpose: Build the central idea that horizontal motion stays constant while vertical motion changes under gravity.
key_visuals: A side view of the projectile path with separate horizontal and vertical motion indicators
Equal spacing in horizontal positions across time, paired with changing vertical spacing
A visual gravity cue pulling downward on the projectile
student_actions: Watch the projectile and compare how its horizontal and vertical motion differ over time
Explain why the horizontal speed stays constant while the vertical speed changes during flight

scenes.scene_name: Changing launch conditions and interpreting outcomes
scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate the relationship between launch parameters and trajectory shape, range, and maximum height.
key_visuals: Multiple trajectories with different angles and speeds over the same ground plane
Markers showing range and peak height for each path
A summary display relating launch angle, speed, and motion outcomes
student_actions: Vary the launch angle and speed and compare the resulting paths
Predict which launch gives the greatest range or highest peak, then verify by observation
